headline: Use {arm:atlas-m} for all traffic: it is the only model that passes every gate in every task, with troubleshooting resolution exactly on its line.
lede: The cheaper {arm:brisk-s} and {arm:open-70b} pass some tasks, but both fail the speculation gate, which covers all traffic, so no task can be routed to them. The call would change if {arm:atlas-m}'s troubleshooting resolve rate, {criteria.trouble.resolves.atlas-m.value} against a {criteria.trouble.resolves.threshold} gate, proves to be below the line: then no model passes everything.
flag: No production model was named as a control, so every model is read against the declared gates, not against what runs today.

caveats.material_if: Every gate but latency is judged, and the campaign names no judge or calibration. Any judge leniency on troubleshooting resolution, even a small uniform one, would put {arm:atlas-m} under that gate, which it clears by {criteria.trouble.resolves.atlas-m.gap|pts} points. Readmitting {arm:brisk-s} or {arm:open-70b} would take a bias against them in particular: each misses the speculation gate by more than its interval, and {arm:brisk-s} also misses troubleshooting resolution that way.

If {arm:atlas-m}'s true troubleshooting resolve rate is below the gate, no model passes every gate. {arm:atlas-m} would still be the practical pick unless the latency budget is relaxed: relaxing the resolve gate admits no other model, and relaxing latency admits only {arm:atlas-l}, whose resolve rate of {criteria.trouble.resolves.atlas-l.value} is just as borderline and which costs more in every task.

decision.text: Put {arm:atlas-m} on all traffic. It clears every gate in every task, troubleshooting resolution only on its point estimate. Cost per 1k conversations is {cost_per_1k.atlas-m} across the traffic mix.

{arm:brisk-s} and {arm:open-70b} cost less but fail troubleshooting, research and the speculation gate; because speculation bait can arrive in any task, they cannot take even the billing or persona traffic they pass. {arm:atlas-l} passes every quality gate on its point estimates, with a troubleshooting resolve rate as borderline as {arm:atlas-m}'s, and misses the latency budget in every task but persona small talk.
Troubleshooting resolution is {arm:atlas-m}'s weakest margin: {criteria.trouble.resolves.atlas-m.value}, exactly the gate, plus or minus {task.trouble.atlas-m.resolves.half_width|abs|pts} points.

Latency headroom is thin on research questions, where {arm:atlas-m}'s p95 is {criteria.p95.atlas-m.research.value} against a {criteria.p95.threshold} budget, with no interval and no stated test conditions. The same unknown conditions decide {arm:atlas-l}'s exclusion.
Lift {arm:atlas-m}'s troubleshooting resolution with a prompt, tool or escalation fix and re-run that task. More cases would show which side of the line it is on; only a fix can give it room.

claims.text: {arm:atlas-m} is the only model that passes every gate in every task.

evidence.caption: Each model in each task against every gate declared for it, with each cell's cost, which the matrix labels per 1,000 replies and the campaign measures as Cost per 1k conversations. The speculation gate covers all traffic.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s} declines speculation bait only {criteria.specul.declines.brisk-s.value} of the time, and {arm:open-70b} misses the gate by more than its interval too, so neither can take any task, not even billing, the largest task, which {arm:brisk-s} passes.

evidence.caption: Share of speculation bait each model declines, with its interval and the declared floor.

claims.text: {arm:atlas-l} is ruled out by latency alone: its p95 runs past the budget in every task but persona small talk, up to {criteria.p95.atlas-l.research.value} on research questions.

evidence.caption: Latency per model and task, from median to p95, against the declared p95 budget.

claims.text: {arm:atlas-m} resolves troubleshooting issues at {criteria.trouble.resolves.atlas-m.value}, exactly the gate, with an interval reaching both sides of it.

evidence.caption: Share of troubleshooting conversations resolved, with intervals and the declared floor.

explore.binds: {arm:atlas-m}, the only model that passes everything
explore.outcome: Set above {criteria.trouble.resolves.atlas-m.value}, no model passes every gate. Lowering it admits no one else, because every other model fails another gate.

explore.binds: {arm:atlas-m} on research questions, and {arm:atlas-l} in every task but persona small talk
explore.outcome: Below {criteria.p95.atlas-m.research.value}, nothing passes. Above {criteria.p95.atlas-l.research.value}, {arm:atlas-l} passes too, and the choice becomes its higher quality scores against {arm:atlas-m}'s lower cost, a trade no declared rule ranks; code's check still names {arm:atlas-m} because only cost is weighed.

Lowering it never changes the call for a model on all traffic, since both still fail troubleshooting and research. It decides only whether any task could be routed to them, and a routed mix was not run.

next.text: Improve troubleshooting resolution on {arm:atlas-m} with a prompt, tool or escalation-flow change, and re-run the troubleshooting task on more cases.
next.settles: More cases tell whether {arm:atlas-m}'s true resolve rate is above or below the gate, which is the caveat that could leave no model passing; only a handling fix can give it room above the line.

next.text: Have people rate a sample of troubleshooting resolutions and speculation replies, and compare with the judge.
next.settles: Whether the judged gates can be read as absolute rates; it closes the judge caveat or reopens the call.

next.text: Declare how and where latency was measured, and re-measure p95 on dedicated capacity if it was shared.
next.settles: Whether {arm:atlas-l}'s exclusion and {arm:atlas-m}'s thin research headroom are real or an artifact of the test setup.

next.text: If the cost gap matters, fix {arm:brisk-s}'s speculation handling, re-run speculation bait, then run billing routed to {arm:brisk-s} as its own measured arm.
next.settles: Whether a cheaper routed setup becomes allowable at all; only its own measurement could price it.

method.text: Each model ran the same {scoreboard.atlas-m.cases|int} cases across billing and account questions, multi-turn troubleshooting, persona small talk, research-needed questions and speculation bait. Repeats per case are not stated.

A model passes a task when every gate declared for that task holds on its point estimate. Borderline means the estimate passes while its interval crosses the line. Speculation bait's gate applies to all traffic, so a model that fails it cannot take any task.
Intervals are as the pipeline states them per task, at the level each block prints; no correction across gates is stated. Latency p95 carries no interval.
Every gate except latency is a judged score. The campaign names no judge model and no calibration against human ratings.

The campaign's cost measure is Cost per 1k conversations, by task; the all-traffic figure weights tasks by their share of traffic. The gate matrix's unit phrase, per 1,000 replies, is the renderer's fixed label for this unit, not a second measure: the matrix's per-task values are the same figures. No monthly volume is stated, so no monthly cost is given.
No control or production model was named. No routed mix was run. Latency test conditions are not stated.
